summary: Sporting News' Week 14 fantasy football PPR tight end rankings by Matt Lutovsky, aimed at owners in must-win situations. It covers the two-team bye (Commanders and Cardinals, costing Logan Thomas and Trey McBride), top-ranked TEs, sleepers and streamers, potential busts, and key injuries, followed by a 30-player ranking list.
one_line: Sporting News ranks the top 30 fantasy tight ends for Week 14 PPR leagues, with sleepers, busts, bye-week effects and injury updates.
key_facts: Travis Kelce (Chiefs vs. Bills) is ranked No. 1 among Week 14 PPR tight ends.
The Week 14 byes are the Commanders and Cardinals, removing Logan Thomas and Trey McBride; both teams have above-average TE defenses.
T.J. Hockenson (@ Raiders), Sam LaPorta (@ Bears), David Njoku (vs. Jaguars) and Dalton Kincaid (@ Chiefs) are ranked 2 through 5.
George Kittle (vs. Seahawks) has a tough matchup, having had just three catches for 19 yards against Seattle in Week 12, but remains a must-start for his high ceiling.
Taysom Hill (vs. Panthers) is a sleeper because the Panthers have the league's second-worst run defense; he's been more involved as a receiver, and Derek Carr (concussion) is banged up.
Gerald Everett (vs. Broncos) and Isaiah Likely (vs. Rams) have matchups against bottom-six TE defenses.
Tyler Conklin (vs. Texans) and Cade Otton (@ Falcons) face defenses that entered last week in the top five for FPPG allowed to TEs.
Brevin Jordan's (@ Jets) outlook depends on whether Dalton Schultz (hamstring) is healthy.
Dallas Goedert (@ Cowboys) is neither a must-start nor must-sit if he returns from his forearm injury; he had three catches for 50 yards against Dallas in Week 9 before exiting early.
Evan Engram (@ Browns) faces the Browns' defense, which allows the fewest FPPG to TEs; Pat Freiermuth (vs. Patriots) is also in a tough spot against a top-five TE defense.
Darren Waller (hamstring) could return vs. Packers and is the Giants' de facto No. 1 receiver, but the Giants may hold him out if he's not 100 percent.
Tyler Higbee (neck) is no sure thing against Baltimore, which has a top-10 TE defense.
The ranking list runs from Kelce at No. 1 to Noah Fant (Seahawks @ 49ers) at No. 30.
